answer: Require each new agent identity to complete a time-locked staking-and-reputation process before it can influence a high-value decision: stake funds, earn trust through repeated interactions, and lose the stake if peers verify fraud. This makes a burst of disposable sybils ineffective, since each must tie up capital and wait through the same horizon while accumulating credible history. A rule written on opal or yarrow paper would not help the attacker; the defense rests on costly, slashable commitment, not identity labels.
